scenarioName: Stab Wound to Chest — Recurrent Tension Pneumothorax

scenarioStory.history: Patient sustained a single stab wound to the left lateral chest during an altercation approximately 10 minutes ago. Initially alert with mild dyspnea; over the past several minutes has become progressively more short of breath and anxious, now with visibly labored breathing.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 29-year-old male with a single stab wound to the left lateral chest, now with worsening respiratory distress, absent left breath sounds, tracheal deviation, JVD, and hypotension. → Needle decompression performed: Crew recognizes tension pneumothorax from the absent left breath sounds, tracheal deviation, JVD, and hypotension in this penetrating chest trauma patient, and performs needle decompression of the left chest. → Symptoms recur, repeat decompression: During transport, the patient's breath sounds diminish again on the left with recurrent tracheal deviation and hypotension. The crew recognizes recurrent tension physiology and repeats needle decompression on the same side per protocol. → Repeat decompression successful: Following the repeat decompression, the patient's breath sounds and hemodynamics improve and remain stable. The crew continues serial reassessment and completes rapid transport to the trauma center.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Stab wound to chest, worsening difficulty breathing

scenarioEvents.name: Needle decompression performed
scenarioEvents.description: Crew recognizes tension pneumothorax from the absent left breath sounds, tracheal deviation, JVD, and hypotension in this penetrating chest trauma patient, and performs needle decompression of the left chest.
relatedChecklist: Needle decompression of left chest, 2nd ICS midclavicular line, for tension pneumothorax
Apply semi-occlusive dressing to the open chest wound
Apply supplemental O2, titrate to maintain SpO2 greater than 94%

scenarioEvents.name: Symptoms recur, repeat decompression
scenarioEvents.description: During transport, the patient's breath sounds diminish again on the left with recurrent tracheal deviation and hypotension. The crew recognizes recurrent tension physiology and repeats needle decompression on the same side per protocol.
relatedChecklist: Serially reassess breath sounds and hemodynamics en route for recurrent tension physiology
Repeat needle decompression of the left chest, same site, for recurrent tension pneumothorax

scenarioEvents.name: Repeat decompression successful
scenarioEvents.description: Following the repeat decompression, the patient's breath sounds and hemodynamics improve and remain stable. The crew continues serial reassessment and completes rapid transport to the trauma center.
relatedChecklist: Continue serial vital sign reassessment; minimize scene time and transport to trauma center

scenarioEvents.name: Decompression delayed
scenarioEvents.description: The crew focuses on the wound dressing and IV access without recognizing the tension pneumothorax. Without decompression, the patient's respiratory distress and hypotension progressively worsen toward obstructive shock.
relatedChecklist: Immediately recognize tension pneumothorax and perform emergent needle decompression of the left chest
